thought.text:
**Mystery solved — it was my own transcription error, not a software problem.** The admin cookie value I'd been hand-typing across all my failing tests was **47 chars**, but the real value in `appsettings.json` is **50 chars** — I had dropped `4242` from the middle (the string contains a repeating `234242342423` sequence). When I use the correctly extracted cookie, the admin UI renders **8/8 consistently**.

The one earlier "ADMIN" render was my very first test, where I *programmatically* extracted the cookie via `sed` (real value) — that's why it worked. Every subsequent test reused my mis-transcribed constant → noadmin. There is no anomaly; the server's auth is correct and stable.

Let me do a final clean validation using the programmatically-extracted (real) cookie, plus confirm the render path and services.

`UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e` (50 chars)

The value I hand-typed was:
`UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e` — wait, these look identical in the display, but the diff shows that position 34 onward is different. Let me look more carefully.

Mine:   `UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e`

`UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e`

U-I-H-2-3-4-d-c-b-j-n-0-9-3-4-7-2-3-d-w-m-Z-S-I-Z-L-2-3-4-2-4-2-3-K-U-O-W-i-d-s-q-w-6-1-2-3-e

UIH234 = 6
dcbjn0 = 12

dwmZSI = 24

423KUO = 36
Widsqw = 42
6123e = 47

Hmm, this is 47. But the file says 50. So the actual value in the file has 3 more characters somewhere. The diff is at position 34: file=4, mine=K.

So at position 34, the file has "4", mine has "K". Let me try reconstructing.

1:U 2:I 3:H 4:2 5:3 6:4 7:d 8:c 9:b 10:j 11:n 12:0 13:9 14:3 15:4 16:7 17:2 18:3 19:d 20:w 21:m 22:Z 23:S 24:I 25:Z 26:L 27:2 28:3 29:4 30:2 31:4 32:2 33:3 34:4(file) / K(mine) ...

So the actual file value is:
`UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL234242342423KUOWidsqw6123e`

Wait, let me redo this. The first 33 characters match: `UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423` — let me recount.

Mine (47 chars): `UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e`

So mine = `UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423` + `KUOWidsqw6123e`
= `UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e`

The file (50 chars) has the same first 33 characters, then at position 34: `42423KUOWidsqw6123e`.

Wait: file positions 34–50 = `4 2 4 2 3 K U O W i d s q w 6 1 2 3 e`. That's 17 characters (34..50 = 17 positions).

So file = `UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423` + `42423KUOWidsqw6123e`
= `UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL234242342423KUOWidsqw6123e`

Let me count: first 33 + 17 = 50.

So the actual value is:
`UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL234242342423KUOWidsqw6123e`

And mine was:
`UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e`

The difference: the file has `234242342423`, mine had `2342423` (I dropped the `4242` — I transcribed "234242342423" as "2342423").

So this is purely my transcription error! The real value has the sequence "234242342423" (which is a repeating pattern "2342" x3 + "423"), and when I read it off the terminal output I dropped part of it and typed "2342423".

So the entire "anomaly" was an artifact of my own hand-typing. The server is working correctly. If I use the real cookie, ADMIN renders consistently (8/8).

That's a big relief. That explains it:
- The first test I did — the one that rendered ADMIN — was when I used the cookie extracted via `sed` from appsettings.json (the REAL value). Let me confirm: yes! The first time I ran `/app with admin cookie` I used `COOKIE=$(sed -n 's/.*"AuthCookie": "\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' appsettings.json)` — the programmatically extracted real value. That's why it rendered ADMIN.
- After that, I hand-typed the cookie `UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e` and reused it — which was wrong (missing characters) — so everything after showed noadmin.

So there is no anomaly at all. The server is working correctly. Authentication is working correctly. The real admin cookie (extracted from appsettings.json) renders the admin UI 8/8.

Excellent. Now I understand. This was a validation artifact, not a software problem.

action.command:
cd /workspace/src/Bovis.Web
REAL=$(sed -n 's/.*"AuthCookie": "\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' appsettings.json)
echo "Using REAL admin cookie (len=${#REAL})"
echo "=== 1. Root page with REAL admin cookie: full admin UI? ==="
curl -s -H "Cookie: bovis_auth_cookie=$REAL" "http://localhost:5195/" -o /tmp/f_root.html
grep -o -E "Bovis Bohrsäulenvisualisierung|nav-item|Liste der Dienste|Administrationsrechten" /tmp/f_root.html | sort -u
echo "=== 2. /app with REAL admin cookie ==="
curl -s -H "Cookie: bovis_auth_cookie=$REAL" "http://localhost:5195/app" -o /tmp/f_app.html
grep -o -E "Bovis Bohrsäulenvisualisierung|nav-item|Liste der Dienste|nothing at this address" /tmp/f_app.html | sort -u
echo "=== 3. Login page (no auth) ==="
curl -s "http://localhost:5195/login" | grep -o -E "Anmeldung|Anmelden" | sort -u
echo "=== 4. /render endpoint (public API) behavior ==="
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "render(no sid): HTTP %{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:5195/render"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "render(sid=new): HTTP %{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:5195/render?sid=new&format=png"
echo "=== 5. Services currently in config.db ==="
sqlite3 config.db "SELECT path, display_name, content_type FROM files WHERE path LIKE 'services/%';" | head
echo "(count: $(sqlite3 config.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM files WHERE path LIKE 'services/%';"))"
echo "=== 6. bovis/hello (public health) ==="
curl -s -w " -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:5195/bovis/hello"
